prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] EN · Dependency audit (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Package" · longest unbreakable word 147px · one-line width 391px
  col 2: header "Version" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 91px
  col 3: header "License" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 77px
  col 4: header "Vulnerabilities" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 103px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 252px · one-line width 468px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Audit English-language dependencies for package identity, version, licensing, vulnerabilities and relevant notes.","reading":"Readers scan package names to find dependencies, then compare versions, licenses and vulnerability status across rows; notes provide context for individual entries.","groups":["Package and Version identify the dependency and release.","License and Vulnerabilities are compact audit fields intended for comparison down their columns.","Notes provides row-specific context and benefits from flexible space."],"keep_intact":["Package identifiers and version strings, especially scoped package names and prerelease versions.","License names, vulnerability counts and the Vulnerabilities header.","Long unbreakable strings in Notes where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Notes prose at natural word boundaries.","Package names at natural break opportunities; the unusually long package row can absorb additional height.","Vulnerability descriptions at natural word boundaries when needed."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[168,112,98,124,217],"idea":"Fit the viewport exactly while preserving the compact audit fields and package identifiers, accepting splits in the longest Notes string."},{"name":"B","widths":[168,112,98,124,273],"idea":"Allow 56px of horizontal overflow to give every column enough text width for its longest unbreakable string."},{"name":"C","widths":[250,112,98,124,300],"idea":"Use a wider scrolling table to give package names and notes more room for natural wrapping while keeping the comparison fields compact."}]}
